endorsements.quote: On a larger scale, the GI-AI4H also prepares the global community to develop environmental guardrails that factor in the environmental impact of health AI (i.e., whether the negative climate effects of AI are localized in LMICs or marginalized communities) before deployment at scale26.

unlisted_practices: Harmonize global regulatory standards for health AI and strengthen cooperation between international regulatory bodies.
Develop efficient compliance programs to help member states, especially lower-resourced settings, adopt health AI regulatory policies.
Establish accountability plans that hold stakeholders across member states responsible for the safe and equitable use of health AI.
Commit to contribute relevant data to a global repository so member states can independently and continuously develop, monitor, and audit health AI tools.
Build a global knowledge base of health AI tools and implementation use cases to help member states judge applicability and minimize population harms or biases.
Consider technical infrastructure, access to healthcare services, and digital literacy levels as pre-implementation factors in health AI implementation plans.
Tailor health AI to local contexts and healthcare settings and build capacity to localize AI models.
Pool resources and establish cooperative agreements across member states to sustain operational support for implemented health AI.
Safeguard data privacy when sharing population data across member states, for example by assigning access permission levels.
Invest in AI workforce development and community engagement and collaboration to prepare member states to deploy health AI equitably and safely.
Engage underrepresented populations to build shared perspectives that build trust, mitigate biases, and harmonize ethics guidance.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/framework article describing strategic priorities for global AI governance established by the WHO Global Initiative on AI for Health.
